design.scope: Joint sensitivity checks of Gaussian sample count (2), initial sigma (3), numerical stopping (4). No Huber, line fitting, theta calibration, significance tests or production setting selection.
design.inputs: Exactly the previously verified 23056 visible-column profiles from four reference images, horizontal step 1 pixel. No new coarse-edge selection or image preprocessing.
design.sample_count_basis: Paper 2015 tests odd N=3..21; 23..61 is the already discussed extension. Neither range boundary is an acceptance rule.

fixed_initialization_arms.basis: Reuse the three previously compared initial widths as an explicit exploratory range, not a paper-prescribed optimum or exhaustive initialization test.
fixed_initialization_arms.A: coarse_response, fixed across all N and sigma arms at a given location
fixed_initialization_arms.mu: coarse_y, fixed across all N and sigma arms
fixed_initialization_arms.simplex_basis: Existing 11-sample implementation step sizes held fixed to avoid changing search size when changing N or initial sigma. These inherited numerical choices are not validated by the paper.
fixed_initialization_arms.limits: Only initial sigma sensitivity is varied; this is not an exhaustive test of all A/mu/simplex initializations.

paper_reproduction_arm.role: Reproduce previous unfiltered output and compare its numerical settings. Not pooled into fixed-start window/initial-sigma effects.

design.iteration_basis: Doubling the inherited 800 cap is an exploratory numerical sensitivity sequence. 6400 is a finite experiment budget, not proof that every solve is sufficient.
design.legacy_stopping: Original objective-only: max f-min f <= 1e-10*(abs(best f)+1e-30), evaluated before the iteration cap.

dual_stopping.parameter_test: max over vertices and A,mu,sigma of abs(q_vertex-q_best)/(1+abs(q_best-origin)) <= tol; origin=(0, coarse_y, 0)
dual_stopping.reason: MathWorks fminsearch documents checking both function and parameter termination. This experiment adds that principle to the existing solver; the scaling and tolerance grid here are explicitly our experiment design, not an exact MATLAB implementation or Fabijanska prescription.
dual_stopping.tolerance_basis: Logarithmically spaced probes ending at the inherited 1e-10, not px thresholds or task-accuracy acceptance limits.

design.objective: Same unweighted SSE, A*exp(-(y-mu)^2/(2*(abs(sigma)+1e-12)^2)); no offset, no position/sigma/amplitude bounds.
design.rejection_policy: None. Keep weak, endpoint, nonconverged, nonpositive-amplitude, large-shift, out-of-image and nonfinite returns. Nonfinite summary statistics are marked unavailable, never silently removed.
design.checkpoint_implementation: One identical simplex trajectory per profile,N,initialization is continued to the strictest pending stopping condition or 6400 steps; all seven conditions retain their own first stop/cap return. Continuing a trajectory does not mutate an already recorded result.
design.reporting: Raw binary64 results for every combination, counts, medians and maxima over all locations. No good-case selection, no best-start merging, no acceptance cutoff. SSE is compared only for the same input sample set.
